card.name: Words after verbs of spatial position
card.fires_on: Small words (your, inside, their, to, in, through, across) right after a verb of placement or extent, in science or teaching text about space and body position. They come where a place or location phrase is about to follow.

modes.label: Body position
modes.description: Possessive or arm word after instructions to put or stick limbs out or at one's sides.
modes.example: For midline letters stick your arms out by<< your>> sides.

modes.label: Path or extent
modes.description: Preposition or helper word after a verb of running, extending or passing, before a place.
modes.example: If it replaced the sun in our solar system it<< would>> extend up to Saturn.

modes.label: Movement through a structure
modes.description: Preposition after a verb of passing or running through or across a physical structure.
modes.example: A rope, cable or belt usually runs<< inside>> the groove.

card.writes: It seems to push toward place and direction continuations and away from the word center.
card.plain: It fires on little words that come just before a place or direction is named, as in 'arms out by your sides'.
